topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's objectives, reviewing histopathology practicals and outlining the genetic and historical concepts to be covered.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and laboratory assays for measuring transformed phenotypes.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer-associated mutations are classified and how allele dosage and specific mutational mechanisms alter protein activity to promote tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the distinct causes of sequence and chromosomal instability, ranging from DNA repair failure to mitotic segregation errors and subsequent cellular stress.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis models and hereditary cancer syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation or inheritance of cancer-predisposing mutations drives tumor progression and disease evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and suggested reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, invites questions, and recommends supplementary reading for the break.
